title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: GPG Person
tiers.description: All directors and senior management (each director, the Managing Director, CFO, COO and Company Secretary), Key Management Personnel, any other person designated by the Board in writing, and employees who work closely with senior management, work in finance/strategy/business development/estimating/IT, or may otherwise come into possession of market sensitive information. Bound by the general insider trading ban (clause 2), Blackout Periods and notification (clause 3), the protection-arrangement, speculative-trading and secured financing/margin lending bans (clause 4), and the exemptions of clause 5.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of GPG's Board; distinguished only for clearance purposes, being authorised by the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee or an Independent Director.

tiers.name: Other directors, Company Secretary and Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, the Company Secretary, and Key Management Personnel; distinguished only for clearance purposes, being authorised by the Chair of the Board or, in their absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Any other GPG Person
tiers.description: Any GPG Person not a director, Company Secretary or KMP (e.g. designated senior employees); distinguished only for clearance purposes, being authorised by the Company Secretary or, in their absence, the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Controlled Entities
tiers.description: A company or trust controlled by a GPG Person. Included in the GPG Person definition without limitation, so bound by every clause of the policy in the same way as the individual.

tiers.name: Associates (clause 3 only)
tiers.description: A spouse (including de facto), child (including step/adopted), close relative, or person financially dependent on or acting in concert with a GPG Person. Included in the GPG Person definition only 'for the purposes of clause 3' (Blackout Periods and notifications), not for clause 4's protection-arrangement, margin lending or security-granting bans.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any GPG Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including GPG's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that GPG Person's behalf

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: GPG, in its sole and absolute discretion and without notice, may impose additional restrictions on trading by any or all GPG Persons or other staff, even outside a Blackout Period; such a restriction must be kept strictly confidential. The Board may also specify further mandated Blackout Periods.

rules.detail: Protection arrangements (which the policy expressly extends to 'GPG products in the derivatives markets') are banned outright at any time in respect of unvested securities.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any GPG securities (or GPG products in the derivatives markets) ... is prohibited at any time in respect of any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Same outright ban applies while vested securities remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Once vested and free of any holding lock, a derivative-based protection arrangement is permitted with prior consent under clause 3.3 from the Authorising Officer.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under clause 3.3.

rules.detail: Instruments that limit the economic risk of a holding (hedging) are a 'protection arrangement', banned outright over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any GPG Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including GPG's securities held beneficially ... is prohibited at any time in respect of any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging remains banned outright while vested securities are subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unlocked securities is permitted with consent under clause 3.3.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under clause 3.3.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a forward sale or similar structure that limits economic risk of the holding falls within 'protection arrangements' and is banned outright over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any GPG Person's security holding ... is prohibited at any time in respect of any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Same outright ban applies while vested securities are subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: A monetisation structure over vested, unlocked securities is caught only as a protection arrangement and needs consent under clause 3.3.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under clause 3.3.

rules.detail: Short selling beyond the GPG Person's holding is named as a form of protection arrangement, banned outright in respect of unvested securities.
rules.evidence: amount to "short selling" of securities beyond the GPG Person's holding of securities

rules.detail: Same outright ban applies to holding-locked vested securities.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Short selling beyond holding is defined narrowly (only where it exceeds the person's own holding); once vested and unlocked it requires consent under clause 3.3.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires consent under clause 3.3.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy and is not captured by the insider trading, protection-arrangement or secured financing provisions.

CFDs are named only as an example of derivative-market instruments caught by the short-term/speculative trading ban (4.1). A CFD used to limit economic risk of a holding is instead a protection arrangement under 4.2 (banned if unvested/holding-locked, otherwise requiring consent under 3.3); a short-term or speculative CFD is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements involving unvested GPG securities are banned outright.
rules.evidence: GPG Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving GPG securities [which are unvested or subject to a holding lock].

rules.detail: Same outright ban applies while vested securities remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: GPG Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly ... grant any form of security ... over any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving GPG securities.

rules.detail: A margin lending arrangement over vested, unlocked GPG securities is permitted with consent under clause 3.3.
rules.evidence: Unless clause 4.3(a) applies, GPG Persons may, directly or indirectly ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving GPG securities, with consent under clause 3.3.

rules.detail: Granting any charge, mortgage, pledge or other security over unvested GPG securities is banned outright.
rules.evidence: GPG Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that GPG Person or any third party.

rules.detail: Same outright ban applies while vested securities remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: grant any form of security ... over any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Granting security over vested, unlocked GPG securities is permitted with consent under clause 3.3.
rules.evidence: Unless clause 4.3(a) applies, GPG Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any of GPG's securities, to secure any obligation of that GPG Person or any third party ... with consent under clause 3.3.

rules.detail: Any secured financing (grant of security to secure an obligation of the GPG Person or a third party) in respect of unvested GPG securities is banned outright — directly on point for a funded collar's loan leg.
rules.evidence: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any GPG securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that GPG Person or any third party.

rules.detail: A loan secured on vested, unlocked GPG securities is permitted with prior consent under clause 3.3 from the Authorising Officer.
rules.evidence: GPG Persons may, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... to secure any obligation of that GPG Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving GPG securities, with consent under clause 3.3.

rules.detail: General ban on short-term or speculative trading, expressly including derivative-market transactions; no fixed holding-period threshold is stated.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should GPG Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in GPG securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in GPG securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets.

acquire securities under any director or employee security plan or through the exercise of options or performance rights under an option or performance rights plan or acquire, or agree to acquire, options or performance rights under an option or performance rights plan.

financing_disclosure: GPG Person — trigger: beginning or ceasing to have a substantial holding in GPG, or a movement of at least 1% while holding a substantial holding — to: Authorising Officer — deadline: not specified (clause 3.3(a)(iv)).

exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer (Chair of ARC/an Independent Director for the Chair of the Board; the Chair of the Board/Chair of ARC for other directors, Company Secretary and KMP; the Company Secretary/Managing Director for any other GPG Person) may, in absolute discretion and without giving reasons, approve dealing during a Blackout Period or otherwise-prohibited dealing in 'exceptional circumstances' (severe financial hardship or a court order/enforceable undertaking). The decision is final and binding, can be withdrawn if new information emerges, and must be kept strictly confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: GPG Persons may at any time ... dispose of GPG securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a lender's enforcement sale as a breach, this exemption lets a bank liquidate collateral shares at any time, including during a Blackout Period, provided the underlying secured financing was itself validly entered into (i.e. over vested, unlocked shares with consent).

bespoke_clauses.clause: for the purposes of clause 3 only, a spouse (including a de facto spouse), child ... a close relative, a person financially dependent on or acting in concert with any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Natural-person associates (spouse, children, dependants) are only brought within clause 3 (Blackout Periods/notification); the express clause 4 bans on protection arrangements and secured financing/margin lending apply only to the GPG Person and entities they control, so a collar or loan booked in a spouse's own name arguably sits outside clause 4's literal wording, though general insider trading law and the acting-in-concert language would still need to be checked case by case.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company or trust controlled by any of the persons referred to in clause 1(b)(i) above
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike natural-person associates, a company or trust the executive controls is included in the GPG Person definition without limitation, so routing the collar/loan through a family trust or investment vehicle does not escape clause 4's bans.

bespoke_clauses.clause: GPG may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on trading ... even where the proposed trade would otherwise take place outside a Blackout Period ... must be kept strictly confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A scheduled collar entry, roll or unwind date can be blocked by an undisclosed ad hoc restriction with no advance warning and no stated end date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If an GPG Person comes into possession of Inside Information after receiving a clearance to trade, they must not trade despite having received the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar or financing transaction can become unexecutable if inside information arises between clearance and signing, with no stated re-clearance mechanism.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer has discretion to approve dealings in GPG securities during a Blackout Period ... may include, without limitation, severe financial hardship, or a requirement to comply with a court order.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Offers a narrow, wholly discretionary and unreviewable route to execute, unwind or settle a collar during a closed period, but cannot be relied upon as a matter of right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If an GPG Person undertakes any of the actions described in paragraph 5(a), that GPG Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even exempt dealings (e.g. a secured lender's enforcement sale) must still be reported to the Authorising Officer after the event, creating an ongoing disclosure trail for any financing arrangement.
There is no minimum shareholding requirement to preserve, simplifying sizing of the collar and loan against the full vested, unlocked holding.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted GenusPlus shares is achievable but only once the shares are both vested and free of any holding lock, and only with prior consent under clause 3.3: the put and call together are a 'protection arrangement' under clause 4.2, and the loan secured on those shares is a 'grant of security'/margin lending arrangement under clause 4.3, each independently banned outright while the shares remain unvested or holding-locked, with no exemption authority for that state. Once vested and unlocked, both legs require consent from the Authorising Officer (varying by seniority: Chair of ARC/Independent Director, the Chair of the Board, or the Company Secretary/Managing Director), execution must avoid the three annual Blackout Periods and any confidential ad hoc restriction, and any clearance lapses if inside information later arises. Usefully, a secured lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly carved out as a permitted dealing 'at any time', so the bank's ability to liquidate collateral is not blocked by a subsequent closed period. Natural-person associates (as opposed to controlled companies or trusts) are, on the policy's literal wording, only caught by the Blackout Period/notification regime and not by clause 4's substantive bans, which may be relevant to structuring but should not be relied on without further analysis. There is no minimum shareholding requirement and no fixed short-term holding period beyond a general speculative-trading ban.
